title: AFAuth agent trust-attestor bindings
description: Schema for the trust-attestor binding file persisted at $AFAUTH_HOME/trust.json (default ~/.afauth/trust.json), written with file mode 0600. Holds the agent's link(s) to one or more trust attestors (AFAP-0006, §10) so a human-on-the-hook signal can be minted on demand. Client-local interop convention, not part of the wire protocol — see spec/storage.md. Readers MUST ignore unknown fields.

version.description: On-disk format version. 2 is canonical: a `bindings` array, so an agent may hold several attestor links at once. Version 1 held a single binding inline at the top level (the same per-binding fields, no `bindings` array); a conformant reader SHOULD migrate a v1 file to v2 on load.

bindings.description: The agent's attestor bindings, keyed logically by base_url. Empty when the agent has linked no attestor.

base_url.description: The attestor's base URL, e.g. https://trust.afauth.org. This is the binding's logical key; a comparison ignores a trailing slash. Re-linking the same base_url replaces the binding in place rather than appending a duplicate.

iss.description: The attestor's issuer identifier — the minted JWT's `iss` claim, e.g. "afauth-trust". This is exactly what a service lists in billing.accepted_attestors (§4.4), so it is the value reconciled before sending an attestation. The attestor does not announce it at link time; it is learned from the first minted token and cached here, so it is absent until the first mint.

agent_did.description: The did:key this binding was minted for. A binding whose agent_did differs from the active key is ORPHANED (e.g. left behind by a key rotation) and MUST NOT be used to mint or send an attestation — the JWT would assert the old DID while requests are signed by the new key. A binding with no recorded agent_did (legacy/hand-edited) is treated as not-orphaned.

binding_id.description: Opaque binding identifier issued by the attestor at link time. There is no bearer token: the agent authenticates mints by signing the attestor's token endpoint with its account key (§3.1 keyless mint).

binding_token_expires_at.description: Unix seconds when the binding lapses if left unused (the inactivity window). The attestor slides this forward on every successful mint; a client SHOULD refresh the cached value from the mint response. 0 means no expiry was reported (treated as not-expired).

verification.description: The strongest human-verification method the attestor reported at the most recent mint. Cached for display (e.g. `afauth status`) without a network call; it MAY lag the attestor since it is refreshed only when a token is minted.

verification_seen_at.description: Unix seconds when `verification` was last refreshed from a mint.
